subject: Routing workshop schedule & load-test windows — working session coordination
messages:
From: Aiden Park <aiden.park@flowops.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Leslie Chen <leslie.chen@flowops.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Hands-on routing policy retreat & load test windows for POC

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at FlowOps is excited to move into a hands-on working session to lock down routing policy decisions for our POC. High-level ask: a two-day, interactive workshop that covers prompt review, model selection for each tier, fallback rules, region routing, and at least one controlled load test run.

Rough attendee list from our side: myself (product), Leslie (infra lead), two SREs who will run traffic, and procurement will join for scheduling/terms follow-up.

Proposed windows (PST):
- Option A: Tue/Wed Nov 18–19, afternoons (13:00–17:00)
- Option B: Mon/Tue Nov 23–24, afternoons (13:00–17:00)

Can your team support both windows? For the load tests we anticipate starting small and ramping: nominally 100 QPS up to ~1k sustained for 15–30 minute runs, tokens per request ~400 average. We can provide sample prompts but would like Redwood to advise on batching/cache settings during the session.

Attaching a short one-pager with asks (POC-ask.pdf).

Thanks — looking forward to firming this up.

—Aiden
Aiden Park
Product Manager, FlowOps
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aiden Park <aiden.park@flowops.com>
Cc: Leslie Chen <leslie.chen@flowops.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hands-on routing policy retreat & load test windows for POC

Hi Aiden / Leslie,

Appreciate the clear asks — this is exactly the kind of hands-on session we enjoy running. We can support both windows in principle but have some constraints around engineering on-call bandwidth that week. To keep things practical, can you confirm which window is preferred? If you pick Nov 23–24 we should have a fuller engineering roster available.

Proposed Redwood agenda (draft):
1) Day 1 — prompt review & model tiering (13:00–17:00)
   - Review representative prompts (bring 8–12)
   - Map prompts to candidate models + quantization recommendations
2) Day 2 — routing policy & controlled load tests (13:00–17:00)
   - Define fallback rules and regional tiering
   - Run 2x controlled load tests (ramp plan, observe latency, test canary fallback)

Pre-reads: I uploaded a short routing playbook and an example agenda to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-routing-workshop (redwood-routing-playbook.pdf). Please drop your sample prompts into the folder ahead of the session; Marcus will use them to build the load test harness.

One operational question: do you expect token lengths to spike beyond 1k for any flows? That changes how we recommend KV cache sizing. Also please confirm the AWS regions you want tested (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-northeast-1?).

We can calendar-block tentatively for Nov 20–21 if you'd like an earlier window, but my recommendation is to target Nov 23–24 for full engineering coverage.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Aiden Park <aiden.park@flowops.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hands-on routing policy retreat & load test windows for POC

Vanessa — looping in engineering details so FlowOps has transparency on what we can support.

Summary of what Marcus & infra can provide:
- Test harness: we will spin up a controlled generator against the selected model variant(s).
- Regions: we can run tests in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. ap-northeast-1 is possible but requires additional time to provision (ok if you pick the other two).
- Ramp plan suggestion: 0 -> 100 QPS over 5 minutes, hold 30m, ramp to 500 QPS over 10 minutes, hold 15m, brief spike to 1k QPS for 5 minutes, then cool down.
- Metrics we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 token latency, GPU utilization, tail latency, request error rate, fallback trigger counts.

Needs from FlowOps (please provide before Nov 20):
- Representative prompt set (CSV) with token estimates
- Expected concurrency targets per route
- Any hard SLO targets (e.g., 95th < 500ms)

Attaching a simple CSV template for load test inputs: loadtest-template.csv.

Operational notes: KV cache behavior matters if your prompts have long prefixes; if many sessions reuse prefixes we can cache to reduce per-token compute. For canary/fallback behavior we recommend a 30s window for degradation detection before switching to a lighter model.

Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Inference Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Leslie Chen <leslie.chen@flowops.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Aiden Park <aiden.park@flowops.com>
Bcc: procurement@flowops.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hands-on routing policy retreat & load test windows for POC

Thanks Vanessa / Marcus.

FlowOps prefers Option B (Nov 23–24) due to travel schedules. A couple of clarifications before we lock calendar invites:
- Can you confirm an on-call Redwood engineer will be available during the late PST window (we may run some validation outside the 13:00–17:00 block depending on results)?
- For the fallback test — can Redwood automatically route to a smaller L3 model when latency spikes, or will that be manual? We'd prefer an automated canary rule if possible.

Estimated traffic for the test day (these are conservative):
- Primary route: 200 QPS sustained for 20 minutes, then ramp to 700 QPS for 10 minutes
- Aux route: 50 QPS sustained
- Avg tokens per request: 420

Attaching attendee spreadsheet: POC-attendees.csv (names + roles). Procurement is on the BCC to coordinate contract language once schedule is final.

If everything looks good we can confirm Nov 23–24.

—Leslie
Leslie Chen
Infra Lead, FlowOps
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aiden Park <aiden.park@flowops.com>, Leslie Chen <leslie.chen@flowops.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Final schedule: Routing workshop & load tests (Nov 23-24)

Hi Aiden / Leslie — confirmed. Final schedule and operational notes below.

Schedule (PST):
- Tue, Nov 23 — Prompt review & model tiering — 13:00–17:00 (Vanessa, Marcus in-room; Sergio on call for platform config)
- Wed, Nov 24 — Routing policy & controlled load tests — 13:00–17:00 (Load tests scheduled 14:00–15:30; Marcus will run the harness; Rishi on-call for fallback/rollbacks)

Confirmed engineering coverage: Marcus (lead), Rishi (fallback/runbook), Sergio (infra provisioning). We will have an on-call rota for the evening if the test requires extended validation — Marcus will stay on remote standby until 19:00 PST both days.

Operational decisions agreed:
- Regions to test: us-west-2 and eu-west-1.
- Canary fallback: Redwood will run an automated canary that switches to the pre-configured lighter model after sustained p95 latency > 1.2s for 30s. This will be tested in the Wednesday run.
- Ramp plan: we'll follow the plan Marcus outlined; FlowOps' estimated traffic (200 -> 700 QPS, aux 50 QPS) looks good.

Pre-work items (please upload by Mon, Nov 22):
- Representative prompt set (CSV)
- Any additional SLO targets you want us to enforce during the run

Attachments: calendar-invite-FlowOps.ics, routing-workshop-agenda.pdf (contains session owners and slide deck links).

Drive link and HubSpot: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-routing-workshop | HS-66231

See you next week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
